nodes.label: Joseph Stalin
nodes.title: General Secretary and Bolshevik leader
nodes.bio: The General Secretary of the Bolshevik Party. He leads the relentless, uncompromising charge for rapid industrialization and the forced collectivization of the peasantry, policies driven by his fanatical Marxist commitments. He operates his vast empire informally, frequently managing highly sensitive state affairs while sunbathing at his Sochi dacha, playing billiards, or hosting late-night dinners. Deeply intellectual and fiercely autodidactic, he reads voraciously, favoring works like The Last of the Mohicans, takes Ivan the Terrible as his explicit historical role model, and demands total, unquestioning dedication from his intimate subordinates.

nodes.label: Nadya Alliluyeva
nodes.title: Stalin's wife and Industrial Academy student
nodes.bio: Stalin's second wife, currently aged thirty-one. Puritanical, deeply earnest, and psychologically fragile, she prides herself heavily on her strict Bolshevik modesty, frequently wearing the dullest, most shapeless dresses and entirely avoiding makeup. Proud of her mixed Gypsy, Georgian, Russian, and German heritage, she is currently enrolled at the Industrial Academy to study synthetic fibers. She desperately attempts to balance the intense, crushing pressure of being an academic student, a mother, and the General Secretary's wife simultaneously, while anxiously preparing for the raucous annual holiday dinner on November 8.

nodes.label: Vyacheslav Molotov
nodes.title: Premier and Stalin's closest ally
nodes.bio: The Premier of the Soviet Union. A steadfast, highly meticulous, and unyielding ally who directly assists Stalin in orchestrating the monumental and brutal economic shifts of the era, including the harsh, unforgiving requisitioning of grain from the countryside. Beyond his immense state duties, he is a central, ubiquitous fixture in the Kremlin's daily social fabric, frequently seen playing tennis with his family and embarking on extended seaside vacations alongside the rest of the supreme leadership.

nodes.label: Polina Molotova
nodes.title: Bolshevik organiser and Molotov's wife
nodes.bio: Molotov's wife. A dark, highly formidable, and always impeccably dressed woman who lives in her own flat within the exact same Kremlin building as the Stalins. She operates highly successfully within the state apparatus, advancing her own career, and remains a prominent, powerful figure orchestrating the elite's social life.

nodes.label: Lazar Kaganovich
nodes.title: Stalin's deputy
nodes.bio: Stalin's primary deputy and a fiercely loyal, uncompromising enforcer of the regime's will. He is heavily and directly involved in the aggressive, violent push to extract resources to finance rapid industrialization. He is highly visible leading punitive expeditions deep into the Siberian and Ukrainian countrysides, ruthlessly searching for grain hidden by desperate, starving peasants.

nodes.label: Klim Voroshilov
nodes.title: Defence Commissar
nodes.bio: The Commissar of Defense and a highly vital crony within the supreme leadership. He shares a deep, informal personal camaraderie with Stalin, frequently accompanying the General Secretary on rustic camping trips, hunting expeditions, and extensive seaside holidays on the Black Sea, actions which cement the macho, hard-drinking culture of the inner court.

nodes.label: Ekaterina Voroshilova
nodes.title: Voroshilov's wife
nodes.bio: Part of the tight social world of Kremlin wives. Her diary remembers the leadership circle as simple, friendly, and unusually intimate.

nodes.label: Anastas Mikoyan
nodes.title: Senior Bolshevik organiser
nodes.bio: Shrewd Armenian Bolshevik who simply walks across the courtyard when he needs Stalin. He is one of the most sociable figures in the Kremlin family.

nodes.label: Grigory Ordzhonikidze
nodes.title: Heavy Industry chief
nodes.bio: A fellow Georgian, a highly powerful Politburo member, and one of Stalin's oldest, closest, and most trusted personal friends. He operates effectively as a 'Bolshevik Prince' within the inner circle, heavily involved in driving the state's massive industrialization efforts while remaining deeply entrenched in the daily social life and political maneuvering of the ruling magnates.

nodes.label: Genrikh Yagoda
nodes.title: Deputy GPU chief
nodes.bio: The Deputy Chairman of the GPU. Described by his contemporaries as a ferret-faced former jeweler's son possessing a Hitlerish mustache, he maintains a highly distinct and eccentric taste for rare orchids, German pornography, and elite literary friendships. He serves as a vital conduit of information, providing Stalin with critical, highly sensitive intelligence regarding internal party plots and the massive, violent turbulence spreading throughout the rural countryside.

nodes.label: Nikolai Bukharin
nodes.title: Party theorist and former ally
nodes.bio: A brilliant, highly regarded Marxist theorist and formerly the absolute darling of the Party. Having previously served as Stalin's powerful co-ruler in the late 1920s, he was politically outmaneuvered and decisively defeated during the bitter factional struggles against the Rightist opposition. Though completely sidelined from ultimate power, he remarkably remains a close, trusted personal friend of Nadya.

nodes.label: Leon Trotsky
nodes.title: War Commissar and chief rival
nodes.bio: Hero of the Civil War and creator of the Red Army. His struggle with Stalin over power and method shapes the political background of chapter 1.

nodes.label: Lev Kamenev
nodes.title: Senior Bolshevik in post-Lenin succession battles
nodes.bio: A prominent Leftist Politburo member who previously entered into an alliance with Stalin to successfully defeat Leon Trotsky, only to be subsequently turned upon and defeated by Stalin himself. He remains a largely marginalized, heavily monitored figure in the highly tense 1932 political landscape.

nodes.label: Grigory Zinoviev
nodes.title: Party leader and factional strategist
nodes.bio: Prominent Bolshevik leader in the power struggle after Lenin. In the early chapters he appears in shifting tactical alignments with both allies and rivals.

nodes.label: Alexei Rykov
nodes.title: Council of People's Commissars chairman
nodes.bio: A former Premier of the Soviet Union and another highly prominent leader of the defeated Rightist faction. Like Bukharin, he co-ruled the state alongside Stalin in the mid-1920s before being politically isolated, outmaneuvered, and comprehensively stripped of his former power.

nodes.label: Nadezhda Krupskaya
nodes.title: Lenin's wife and Bolshevik educator
nodes.bio: Long-time revolutionary and Lenin's companion in exile and power. Her role in Lenin's final political period is part of the succession context behind the early chapters.

nodes.label: Valerian Kuibyshev
nodes.title: Economics chief
nodes.bio: The state's chief of economics. Despite holding immense, crushing administrative responsibilities managing the frantic industrial push across the Soviet Union, he consistently maintains the highly disheveled appearance of a mad poet. He is widely known and tolerated among the inner court for his great, unapologetic enthusiasm for heavy drinking, pursuing women, and writing poetry.

nodes.label: Nikita Khrushchev
nodes.title: Young party organiser
nodes.bio: A highly energetic, deeply ambitious lower-level party official. He actively attempts to build his network by accompanying highly prominent figures like Molotov, Kaganovich, and his close personal friend Yezhov to various elite gatherings.

nodes.label: Alexander Poskrebyshev
nodes.title: Stalin's chief aide
nodes.bio: Stalin's tirelessly dedicated, highly organized chef de cabinet. He functions as the ultimate gatekeeper to the General Secretary, managing the massive, crushing flow of bureaucratic paperwork, intelligence reports, and scheduling that sustains the dictatorship.

nodes.label: Abel Yenukidze
nodes.title: Kremlin administrator and Nadya's godfather
nodes.bio: Known highly affectionately throughout the court as 'Uncle Abel.' He is the powerful Secretary of the Central Executive Committee, a fellow Georgian, a widely noted bon viveur, and proudly serves as Nadya's godfather, perfectly bridging the gap between sterile state bureaucracy and warm familial intimacy.

nodes.label: Semyon Budyonny
nodes.title: Cavalry commander
nodes.bio: A highly famous, heavily mustachioed Marshal of the Soviet Union and a prominent civil war cavalry hero. He remains a powerful ally of Stalin and is frequently seen posing confidently at events, usually surrounded by crowds of swooning women.

nodes.label: Mikhail Kalinin
nodes.title: Head of state
nodes.bio: The nominal head of state, affectionately known within the intimate circle as Papa Kalinin. Though lacking the raw, unbridled power of Stalin's closest deputies, he is a constant, steady presence at official state functions and informal Kremlin gatherings, serving as a highly visible and reliable ally to the General Secretary.

nodes.label: Keke Djugashvili
nodes.title: Stalin's mother
nodes.bio: Formidable mother who threw out Stalin's violent father and pushed her son toward schooling. Her toughness is part of the childhood world chapter 1 describes.

nodes.label: Kato Svanidze
nodes.title: Stalin's first wife
nodes.bio: Gentle Georgian from another Bolshevik family and Stalin's first wife. Their brief marriage gives Stalin his first son, Yakov.

nodes.label: Yakov Djugashvili
nodes.title: Stalin's elder son
nodes.bio: Stalin's twenty-five-year-old son from his brief first marriage to Kato Svanidze. Having been brought up distantly in Georgia, he permanently joined his highly intimidating father in Moscow in 1921 and constantly attempts to navigate a deeply strained, incredibly difficult relationship with him.

nodes.label: Vasily Stalin
nodes.title: Stalin's son
nodes.bio: Stalin and Nadya's eleven-year-old son. He is explicitly described by his highly critical father as a diminutive, stubborn, and distinctly nervous boy. His ongoing academic studies, particularly his repeated struggles with the German language, are a constant source of profound parental anxiety and detailed correspondence.

nodes.label: Svetlana Stalin
nodes.title: Stalin's daughter
nodes.bio: Stalin and Nadya's seven-year-old daughter. A freckled, energetic red-haired girl who proudly sports a Young Pioneers' uniform. She frequently holidays with her powerful father at his retreat in Sochi, serving as a highly rare, genuinely innocent source of domestic warmth for the terrifying leadership.

nodes.label: Anna Alliluyeva Redens
nodes.title: Nadya's sister
nodes.bio: Nadya's sister, present in family scenes from the Revolution to the last evening in the prologue.

nodes.label: Vissarion Djugashvili
nodes.title: Stalin's father
nodes.bio: Cobbler father whose drinking and violence dominate Stalin's early home life.

nodes.label: Vladimir Lenin
nodes.title: Bolshevik leader
nodes.bio: Founder of the Bolshevik state and Stalin's political hero. He relies on Stalin in crisis, then grows alarmed by Stalin's accumulating power.

nodes.label: Artyom Sergeev
nodes.title: Adopted son in the Stalin household
nodes.bio: The officially adopted son of Stalin and Nadya. He is seamlessly and lovingly integrated into the chaotic household alongside Vasily and Svetlana, perfectly reflecting the highly common Bolshevik practice of adopting and raising the orphaned children of fallen revolutionary comrades.

nodes.label: Pavel Alliluyev
nodes.title: Red Army officer
nodes.bio: Nadya's brother. He currently serves as a high-ranking Commissar for the Red Army stationed abroad in Berlin. He frequently returns to the tense atmosphere of Moscow bringing a literal treasure chest of rare foreign gifts for his relatives, maintaining highly strong, affectionate familial ties within the dense Kremlin complex.

nodes.label: Sergei Alliluyev
nodes.title: Electrical worker and Bolshevik supporter
nodes.bio: Skilled electrician and veteran Bolshevik sympathiser whose home becomes a shelter for revolutionaries. His family forms one of Stalin's most important early personal networks.

nodes.label: Olga Alliluyeva (née Fedorenko)
nodes.title: Nadya's mother
nodes.bio: Strong-willed mother at the center of the Alliluyev household. Her home links family life, revolutionary politics, and the emotional world around Nadya.

nodes.label: Fyodor Alliluyev
nodes.title: Bolshevik aide and Nadya's brother
nodes.bio: Nadya's brother who questions Stalin in 1917, works in his Commissariat, and later goes with him to Tsaritsyn.

nodes.label: Alexander Yegorov
nodes.title: Red Army commander
nodes.bio: Red Army commander who served with Stalin in the Polish campaign. His family appears in the social world of the 1932 dinner.

nodes.label: Galina Yegorova
nodes.title: Film actress and Yegorov's wife
nodes.bio: Glamorous actress and wife of Alexander Yegorov. Stalin's flirtation with her helps trigger Nadya's anger during the prologue.

nodes.label: Carolina Til
nodes.title: Housekeeper in the Stalin apartment
nodes.bio: Housekeeper in Stalin and Nadya's Kremlin apartment. She discovers Nadya the next morning and raises the alarm.

nodes.label: Mikhail Tukhachevsky
nodes.title: Western Front commander
nodes.bio: Brilliant commander on the Western Front in 1920. Stalin's refusal to release cavalry to him becomes one of the major quarrels of the Polish campaign.

nodes.label: Alexander "Alyosha" Svanidze
nodes.title: Banking official and Stalin's brother-in-law
nodes.bio: A highly placed Georgian banking official and the biological brother of Stalin's late first wife, Kato. He physically represents the enduring, deeply rooted Georgian familial and cultural ties that the General Secretary actively maintains within the Russian capital.

nodes.label: Maria Svanidze
nodes.title: Opera singer in Stalin's in-law circle
nodes.bio: Alyosha's wife. She is a highly cultured Jewish Georgian opera singer and a remarkably avid, observant diarist who meticulously records the nuanced social interactions, slights, and alliances of the elite inner circle for posterity.

nodes.label: Stanislas Redens
nodes.title: Secret policeman and Anna's husband
nodes.bio: Anna Alliluyeva's husband and Nadya's brother-in-law. He links the Alliluyev family to the security world that increasingly surrounds Stalin's household.

nodes.label: Karl Pauker
nodes.title: Security chief in Stalin's entourage
nodes.bio: Former Budapest Opera barber turned security chief in Stalin's entourage. On the night of the prologue he is one of the first men the frightened household turns to.

nodes.label: Nikolai Vlasik
nodes.title: Bodyguard in Stalin's protective ring
nodes.bio: A highly trusted General who operates as Stalin's primary, ubiquitous personal bodyguard. He is a constant, shadowy presence behind the General Secretary at all times, managing the massive logistical and security requirements of the leader's household and travel.

nodes.label: Yevgenia "Zhenya" Alliluyeva
nodes.title: Actress and Pavel's wife
nodes.bio: Pavel's wife and Nadya's glamorous sister-in-law. She is a highly successful actress who elegantly navigates the upper echelons of Soviet social life, contributing significantly to the dense, interconnected, and highly visible nature of the extended Alliluyev family network.

nodes.label: Andrei Andreyev
nodes.title: Central Committee secretary and Kremlin magnate
nodes.bio: A prominent Politburo member and Central Committee Secretary. Married to Dora Khazan, he effectively bridges the gap between the ultimate political power of the inner circle and the intimate social network surrounding Nadya.

nodes.label: Dora Khazan
nodes.title: Deputy textiles official and Nadya's close friend
nodes.bio: Serving as the Deputy Textiles Minister, she is a highly capable administrator and crucially functions as Nadya Alliluyeva's closest, most trusted personal friend, providing an essential emotional outlet within the high-pressure environment.

nodes.label: Lavrentiy Beria
nodes.title: Emerging security official
nodes.bio: An emerging, highly ambitious, and deeply calculating official hailing from the Caucasus. Desperate to prove his overriding usefulness and ingratiate himself with the supreme leadership in Moscow, he aggressively utilizes the holiday seasons at the Black Sea to gain personal favor, even going so far as to offer to manually weed the gardens at Stalin's Sochi dacha.

nodes.label: Maxim Gorky
nodes.title: Celebrated Russian novelist
nodes.bio: A highly celebrated, globally famous Russian novelist who functions as a cultural centerpiece for the regime. He is heavily courted by the leadership and is frequently seen taking intimate, highly publicized tea with Stalin to project an aura of intellectual sophistication.

nodes.label: Bronislava Poskrebysheva
nodes.title: Doctor and socialite
nodes.bio: A well-educated, highly intelligent doctor who is widely noted for being exceedingly pretty and glamorous. Married to Alexander Poskrebyshev, she is actively and highly successfully integrated into the elite social circles of the Kremlin.

nodes.label: Nikolai Yezhov
nodes.title: Rising security official
nodes.bio: A rapidly rising, highly ambitious figure within the security apparatus affectionately nicknamed "Blackberry" by his peers. He is currently networking heavily with the supreme magnates, maneuvering quietly but efficiently for greater operational power.

nodes.label: Yevgenia Yezhova
nodes.title: Editor and socialite
nodes.bio: Nikolai Yezhov's wife. She is a highly successful editor and a prominent, glamorous socialite who regularly entertains powerful friends, deeply embedding her husband into the vital social fabric of the Kremlin elite.

nodes.label: Andrei Zhdanov
nodes.title: Politburo member and Leningrad boss
nodes.bio: A highly powerful Politburo member serving as the political boss of Leningrad. Known as 'the Pianist' for his musical abilities, he is a deeply trusted friend of Stalin who heavily influences state cultural and ideological policy.
